_status: Module 3, Lesson 3.1, 'IDS and IPS: the alarm and the guard' and 'Filter outbound traffic too' (learner guide of 21 October 2026). Fictional office; 198.51.100.x and 203.0.113.x are documentation address ranges.
title: IDS tells, IPS stops

steps.title: A known attack arrives
steps.text: A request to the portal carries a known attack pattern. A **signature-based** system recognizes it, the way antivirus recognizes a known virus.

ask.q: With an IDS only, what happens to the request?
options: It gets through, and an alert is raised
Nothing: an IDS only works at night
ask.why: An IDS watches and raises an alert. It does not block: someone must act on the alert.

steps.title: IDS tells
steps.text: The request reaches the portal, and Ana's screen shows the alert. An IDS is only as good as the person who reads its alerts.

steps.title: IPS stops
steps.text: An intrusion prevention system sits in the path of the traffic. When it finds the same pattern, it **blocks** the request as well as raising the alert.

steps.title: Nothing known, but something unusual
steps.text: At 2:00 AM the backup server starts sending a large amount of data to an address abroad, two nights in a row. No known attack pattern: it is the **behaviour** that is wrong.

ask.q: Which control was built to catch this?
options: An IDS alert on outbound traffic, and outbound filtering
ask.why: Anomaly-based detection looks for unusual behaviour, and outbound filtering lets servers reach approved destinations only.

steps.title: Without outbound filtering, it leaves
steps.text: If the firewall only watches traffic coming in, the data walks out. The anomaly-based IDS still raises the alarm.

screen.title: Anomaly alert · 02:00
lines: Never seen before at this hour

steps.title: Filter outbound traffic too
steps.text: The server zone may reach approved update sites only, nothing else on the internet. The same transfer is blocked, logged, and reported.

verdict.text: A server that suddenly sends data to an unknown address is a warning sign.

tracks.label: Both raise false alarms
tracks.desk: Report security alerts and odd behaviour on your computer at once.
tracks.it: Tune the IDS and IPS, review the logs on a schedule, and keep them: they feed monitoring and, after an incident, the incident report.

steps.title: IT tunes them
steps.text: A large, legitimate upload at month-end also looks unusual. IT tunes the rules so real alarms stand out, and keeps the logs.

head: What it does
Kinds
rows: Watches traffic or a computer and raises an alert
**Network-based** systems watch traffic; **host-based** ones watch a single computer or server
Can also block what it finds
**Signature-based** looks for known attacks; **anomaly-based** looks for unusual behaviour, such as a large transfer at 2:00 AM
Raise false alarms, so IT tunes them
Their logs feed monitoring and, after an incident, the incident report
